subject: Altitude & Decompression
stem: PLACEHOLDER: Which type of hypoxia results from a reduced partial pressure of inspired oxygen at altitude?
explanation: Hypoxic hypoxia is caused by decreased alveolar PO2 (e.g., altitude). Hypemic = reduced O2-carrying capacity; stagnant = reduced perfusion; histotoxic = impaired cellular utilization.

optionNotes.A: Correct: low inspired PO2 at altitude is hypoxic hypoxia.
optionNotes.B: Wrong: hypemic means reduced oxygen-carrying capacity (anemia, CO).
optionNotes.C: Wrong: stagnant means reduced blood flow (e.g. sustained G).
optionNotes.D: Wrong: histotoxic means cells cannot use oxygen (e.g. cyanide).

subject: Occupational Lung Disease
stem: PLACEHOLDER: Eggshell calcification of hilar nodes is most characteristic of which exposure?
explanation: Silicosis classically shows eggshell calcification of hilar lymph nodes.

subject: Biostatistics
stem: PLACEHOLDER: A screening test has 90% sensitivity and 80% specificity in a population with 10% prevalence. What is the positive predictive value?
explanation: Per 1000 people: 100 diseased, 90 TP; 900 healthy, 180 FP. PPV = 90 / (90+180) = 33%.

subject: Human Factors & Fatigue
stem: PLACEHOLDER: Which countermeasure is best supported for reducing fatigue-related errors in rotating night-shift workers?

options.text: Strategic napping and scheduled bright-light exposure

explanation: Strategic naps and timed light exposure help circadian adaptation and alertness; the other options worsen sleep or performance.
